_comment: Hand-written wording for the API reference, layered over the generated spec (scripts/openapi.mjs). Key: "METHOD /path" exactly as in api-routes.json. Fields: summary, description (shown above the generated text), tag. A key for a route that no longer exists fails npm run docs:openapi -- --check.

GET /api/epg.description: The programmes of one guide in a time window. Pass `channelId` or `eventId`, plus `from` and `to` (ISO 8601).

POST /api/epg/:id/convert.summary: Convert an aired programme to VOD
POST /api/epg/:id/convert.description: Runs the same conversion the scheduler runs after a programme airs. Answers 409 if it is already converted or in progress.

POST /api/epg/copy-day.summary: Copy a day's schedule to other days

GET /api/docs/session.description: Issues a short-lived pass to this documentation site for the signed-in user. Used by the Documentation button in Volt.

GET /api/events/:id/access-check.summary: Check what a viewer elsewhere would get
GET /api/events/:id/access-check.description: What the play gate gives a viewer in `country` (two-letter code) for this event right now, and the layer that decided it: the account's geo, the access rules or the programme. `viewer` is `anonymous` (default), `member` or `entitled`. Same answer as `GET /api/channels/{id}/access-check`.

GET /api/events/:id/inputs/:inputId/prev.summary: Preview one of the event's inputs
GET /api/events/:id/inputs/:inputId/prev.description: A relayed preview address for one of the event's http or https inputs, for sources that refuse playback from other sites. The address is a token that expires after two hours and plays that input only. A push input (SRT, RTMP) answers `400`.

POST /api/events/:id/health/reset.description: Resets the event's health to a clean slate: earlier faults stay in the event log but no longer decide its status, and a stopped event's auto connect give-up is cleared. A fault that is still real is reported again by its next event. Answers with the status before and after. Needs `events: operate`.

POST /api/events/:id/reset-health.description: The same as `POST /api/events/{id}/health/reset`, at the path channels use, so one path works for either kind.

tags._comment: Usage statement per API service (tag): what it is for, key tasks, credential. Required for every service; npm run docs:openapi -- --check fails without one. hidden: true leaves the service out of the customer reference.

Access.description:
A light check that tells your app whether a viewer may play an asset, without issuing a playback token.

**Use it to:**
- Grey out or badge items on catalogue and browse screens with `POST /api/public/access/check`
- Decide whether to show a sign-in or purchase prompt before the viewer presses play

**Credential:** publishable key.

**Good to know:** this endpoint answers yes or no only. To actually start playback, call `POST /api/public/availability`, which returns the playback token. `POST /api/access/check` is an older alias of the same check.

Access Roles.description:
Access roles are named sets of access levels per feature (view, operate, manage) that your admin users inherit.

**Use it to:**
- List default and custom roles with `GET /api/access-roles`
- Build a role editor from the feature list in `GET /api/access-roles/catalogue`
- Create, edit or delete custom roles with `POST /api/access-roles` and `PATCH /api/access-roles/{id}`
- Start from a default role with `POST /api/access-roles/{id}/copy`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `access: view` (or `users: view`) to read and `access: manage` to change.

**Good to know:** default roles cannot be edited, copy them instead. You can only grant levels you hold yourself, and members get the new access on their next request.

Account Settings.description:
Account settings hold your account's own branding: a logo and a primary and secondary colour shown on outward-facing pages such as share pages.

**Use it to:**
- Read the current branding with `GET /api/account-settings`
- Change the logo or colours with `PATCH /api/account-settings`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key. Any signed-in admin user can read, `settings: manage` is needed to change.

**Good to know:** the logo must be an image-library path or an https address. Every change is recorded in the audit log.

Addons.description:
Add-ons are the external services you connect to Volt workflows, and the triggers that decide when Volt sends work to them.

**Use it to:**
- Register, update or remove an add-on with `POST /api/addons` and `PATCH /api/addons/{id}`
- Rotate an add-on's secret with `POST /api/addons/{id}/rotate-secret` and check it with `POST /api/addons/{id}/test`
- Attach add-ons to workflow events with `GET /api/addons/triggers` and `POST /api/addons/triggers`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key. Any signed-in admin user can read, `settings: manage` is needed to change.

**Good to know:** secrets are never returned once set. Follow the resulting runs in the Workflows service.

Analytics.description:
Analytics collects playback beacons from your players and reports audience, usage and per-asset viewing for your account.

**Use it to:**
- Send viewing beacons from a player with `POST /api/public/analytics/beacon`
- Read reports with `GET /api/analytics/overview`, `GET /api/analytics/realtime`, `GET /api/analytics/audience` and `GET /api/analytics/asset`
- See billable usage with `GET /api/analytics/usage`
- Set how long analytics data is kept with `PUT /api/analytics/retention`

**Credential:** playback token for beacons. Reports use an admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `analytics: view` to read and `analytics: manage` to change retention.

**Good to know:** beacon values are bounded, so send what the player measured rather than accumulated totals.

Apps.description:
Apps are the players, websites and mobile apps that publish your content, and each one carries the publishable keys used in public API calls.

**Use it to:**
- Register an app and receive its publishable key (`pk_…`) with `POST /api/apps`
- List and edit apps with `GET /api/apps` and `PUT /api/apps/{id}`
- Issue or revoke keys with `POST /api/apps/{id}/keys` and `DELETE /api/apps/keys/{keyId}`
- Issue an account secret key (`sk_live_…`) for your servers with `POST /api/apps/secret-keys`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `apps: view` to read and `apps: manage` to change. Secret keys also need the admin tier.

**Good to know:** keys are shown once, at creation. Never put a secret key in an app or web page.

Audit.description:
The audit log records who did what in your account, including deletes, so you can review and export changes.

**Use it to:**
- Search the log by action, record type, person and date range with `GET /api/audit`
- Fill filter menus from `GET /api/audit/facets`
- Export matching rows as CSV with `GET /api/audit/export.csv`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, any signed-in admin user.

**Good to know:** the CSV export is capped at 50,000 rows, so narrow the date range for larger periods.

Auth.description:
Auth signs people in to Volt: your admin users to the console and API, and your viewers to your apps, including two-step sign-in.

**Use it to:**
- Sign admin users in and out with `POST /api/auth/login`, `POST /api/auth/refresh` and `POST /api/auth/logout`, and read their access with `GET /api/auth/me`
- Sign viewers in with `POST /api/public/auth/login` or `POST /api/public/auth/register`, and reset passwords with `POST /api/public/auth/password-reset`
- Complete two-step sign-in with the `mfa/challenge/send` and `mfa/challenge/verify` requests
- Use your own identity provider through `POST /api/public/auth/token-exchange`

**Credential:** none to sign in (publishable key for viewers), then admin session or viewer session. Token exchange needs the account secret key.

**Good to know:** call token exchange from your server only, never from an app.

Availability.description:
The play gate decides whether an asset or stream may be played here and now, explains why not, and issues the short-lived playback token.

**Use it to:**
- Check anonymous playback with `GET /api/public/availability`
- Check playback for a signed-in viewer, using their groups and entitlements, with `POST /api/public/availability`
- Pass the returned playback token to the player and to analytics beacons

**Credential:** publishable key, with a viewer session optional.

**Good to know:** the anonymous GET is cached at the edge per app, asset and country, the signed-in POST is never cached. `/api/availability` is an older alias.

Channels.description:
Channels are your 24/7 linear streams: their sources, output, on-air state, redundancy and timeline.

**Use it to:**
- Create and configure channels with `POST /api/channels` and `PATCH /api/channels/{id}`
- Start, stop and put a channel on air with `POST /api/channels/{id}/start`, `.../stop` and `.../air`
- Set filler, auto connect and run failover or test-stream checks with `POST /api/channels/{id}/filler`, `.../auto-connect` and `.../failover-test`
- Read coverage, history, timeline, dayparts and thumbnails with `GET /api/channels/{id}/timeline` and related requests

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `channels: view` to read, `channels: operate` to start, stop or air, and `channels: manage` to change. Radio stations need the same `radio` level.

**Good to know:** creating a channel counts against your group's channel limit. Check `GET /api/channels/{id}/delete-impact` before deleting.

Daypart Presets.description:
Daypart presets are ready-made ways of dividing a broadcast day into labelled parts (such as breakfast or prime time) for a channel's timeline.

**Use it to:**
- List the available presets with `GET /api/daypart-presets`
- Apply a preset or your own dayparts to a channel with `PUT /api/channels/{id}/dayparts`
- Read a channel's current dayparts with `GET /api/channels/{id}/dayparts`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `channels: view`. Applying dayparts to a channel needs `channels: manage`.

**Good to know:** dayparts label the channel timeline only. They do not change the schedule or what goes to air.

Discovery.description:
The starting point of the API: a service document that links to every collection, plus reference lists and health checks.

**Use it to:**
- Start at `GET /api` and follow links instead of hard-coding paths (send `Accept: application/ld+json` for the hypermedia form)
- Read the vocabulary with `GET /api/context.jsonld` and `GET /api/doc`
- Fill pickers from `GET /api/caption-languages` and `GET /api/ingest-protocols`
- Check the service with `GET /health` and `GET /health/ready`

**Credential:** none.

Docs.description:
Opens this documentation site for a signed-in admin user by issuing a short-lived pass.

**Use it to:**
- Get a documentation link for the current user with `GET /api/docs/session`
- Back a Documentation button in your own admin tools, sending the user to the returned URL before it expires

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer), any signed-in admin user. Account secret keys are refused because documentation access is for people.

EPG.description:
The EPG holds the programme schedule for each channel and event, including geo rules, slot replacement and automatic VOD after airing.

**Use it to:**
- Read a guide window with `GET /api/epg` (pass `channelId` or `eventId`, plus `from` and `to`) and now and next with `GET /api/epg/now-next`
- Add, edit and repeat programmes with `POST /api/epg`, `PATCH /api/epg/{id}`, `POST /api/epg/series` and `POST /api/epg/copy-day`
- Import XMLTV guides with `POST /api/epg/import/sources` and export them with `GET /api/epg/xmltv` or partner feeds
- Check overlaps with `GET /api/epg/conflicts` and convert an aired programme with `POST /api/epg/{id}/convert`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `epg: view` to read, `epg: operate` to run imports and `epg: manage` to change.

**Good to know:** overlaps are reported, not blocked, so check conflicts after bulk changes.

Encode Profiles.description:
Encoding profiles are the individual renditions Volt can produce, and ladders group them into the set a source is encoded to.

**Use it to:**
- Create and edit renditions with `POST /api/encode-profiles` and `PATCH /api/encode-profiles/{id}`
- Build ladders and set their members in order with `POST /api/encode-profiles/ladders` and `PUT /api/encode-profiles/ladders/{id}/members`
- Preview what a given source would receive with `GET /api/encode-profiles/ladders/{id}/preview`
- See the live profiles with `GET /api/encode-profiles/live-profiles`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key. Any signed-in admin user can read, `settings: manage` is needed to change.

**Good to know:** a ladder that follows a live output profile shows that profile's rungs rather than its own.

Engines.description:
Engines are the encoding and processing engines available to your account, with what each one can do.

**Use it to:**
- List engines and their capabilities with `GET /api/engines` and `GET /api/engines/{id}`
- Check a profile or job against an engine before using it with `POST /api/engines/{id}/validate`
- Choose the engine for an output profile with `PUT /api/engines/profiles/{profileId}`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key. Any signed-in admin user can read, `settings: manage` is needed to validate or change.

Events.description:
Events are scheduled, time-bounded live streams such as a match or a concert, provisioned automatically for their scheduled window.

**Use it to:**
- Schedule and edit events with `POST /api/events` and `PATCH /api/events/{id}`
- Start or stop an event by hand with `POST /api/events/{id}/start` and `.../stop`
- Set filler and auto connect with `POST /api/events/{id}/filler` and `.../auto-connect`
- Review what happened with `GET /api/events/{id}/history`
- Check what a viewer in another country gets with `GET /api/events/{id}/access-check`, and clear old faults with `POST /api/events/{id}/health/reset`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `events: view` to read, `events: operate` to start, stop or clear QC and `events: manage` to change.

**Good to know:** auto connect only decides whether a running event resumes after a restart. The schedule still decides when it runs.

Files.description:
The image library stores your account's images (posters, logos, artwork) and reads their embedded metadata so you can find and reuse them.

**Use it to:**
- Upload, rename, tag and delete images with `POST /api/files`, `PATCH /api/files/{id}` and `DELETE /api/files/{id}`
- Browse folders with `GET /api/files/folders` and create them with `POST /api/files/folders`
- Search names, tags, places and descriptions with `GET /api/files/search`
- Re-read EXIF, IPTC and XMP metadata with `POST /api/files/{id}/metadata/refresh`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key. Any signed-in admin user can read, `media: manage` is needed to change.

**Good to know:** uploading to a path that already exists answers 409. Render sized versions through the Images service.

Filler Assets.description:
Slates (still images) and loops (short videos) are what a channel, station or event shows when every source is lost. Loops & Fillers is the one place they are kept.

**Use it to:**
- List filler assets, each with the streams that use it (`used_by`), with `GET /api/filler-assets`
- Register an asset and get an upload address with `POST /api/filler-assets`
- Mark it ready or rename it with `PATCH /api/filler-assets/{id}`, and remove it with `DELETE /api/filler-assets/{id}`
- Find streams whose fallback is still an Image Library image or a pasted address with `GET /api/filler-assets/elsewhere`
- Copy an Image Library slate in, moving every stream that uses it, with `POST /api/filler-assets/copy-from-library`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `media: view` to read and `media: manage` to change.

**Good to know:** point a channel or event at an asset with `fillerAssetId` on `PATCH /api/channels/{id}` or `PATCH /api/events/{id}`; it must be a ready asset in the same account. Deleting an asset that streams use is refused with `409` and the streams named, unless you add `force=true`.

Fleet.description:
Fleet shows the servers carrying your live work right now and the billable streaming time you have used.

**Use it to:**
- See running hosts, their streams and latest load with `GET /api/fleet/hosts` and `GET /api/fleet/hosts/{id}/samples`
- Read usage for today, this month and per period with `GET /api/fleet/usage`
- Break usage down for one stream with `GET /api/fleet/usage/stream/{id}`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `fleet: view`.

**Good to know:** usage is measured in time. Any cost figure is indicative only.

Groups.description:
Channel groups tie channels, stations and events to an output profile and give each group its share of your plan's channel limits.

**Use it to:**
- List groups with `GET /api/groups`
- Create, rename or remove a group with `POST /api/groups`, `PATCH /api/groups/{id}` and `DELETE /api/groups/{id}`
- See how much of its allocation a group is using with `GET /api/groups/{id}/usage`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key. Any signed-in admin user can read, `settings: manage` is needed to change.

**Good to know:** new items start in the default group, which cannot be removed. A group can only be removed when nothing is in it.

Image delivery.description:
Image delivery serves resized, cropped and converted versions of your library images from signed URLs, cached at the edge.

**Use it to:**
- Use URLs from `POST /api/images/sign` (or built with your signing key) as `GET /img/*` in pages, players and apps
- Check an image exists, without downloading it, with `HEAD /img/*`

**Credential:** none, the signature in the URL is the authorisation.

**Good to know:** responses are immutable, so change the options or path to get a new version rather than expecting a refresh.

Images.description:
The image service resizes, crops and converts library images on the fly, and this service signs the URLs that request those renders.

**Use it to:**
- Turn render options (size, fit, crop, focus, format) into a signed URL with `POST /api/images/sign`
- Get your account's signing key to build URLs locally with `GET /api/images/signing-key`
- Read limits, formats and the base URL with `GET /api/images/config`, and counters with `GET /api/images/stats`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, any signed-in admin user.

**Good to know:** keep the signing key on your servers. It only signs your own account's images.

Ingest.description:
Ingest decides what happens to incoming media files: naming, folder structure, duplicates, required metadata and how the bytes are transferred.

**Use it to:**
- Set the rules ladder with `GET /api/ingest/rules` and `POST /api/ingest/rules`, and see the defaults with `GET /api/ingest/baseline`
- Ask what would happen to a file before it moves with `POST /api/ingest/preview`
- Pull files from linked Dropbox, OneDrive or Google Drive accounts with `POST /api/ingest/providers` and `POST /api/ingest/remote`
- Release held assets with `GET /api/ingest/held` and `POST /api/ingest/assets/{id}/metadata`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `settings: view` to read and `settings: manage` to change.

**Good to know:** remote ingest answers 202 with a job id, so follow it in the Jobs service.

Jobs.description:
Jobs track long-running work in your account, such as conversions and remote ingest, with progress and a reason when something fails.

**Use it to:**
- List and filter jobs with `GET /api/jobs`
- Follow one job's progress and result with `GET /api/jobs/{id}`
- Retry a failed job or cancel one in progress with `POST /api/jobs/{id}/retry` and `POST /api/jobs/{id}/cancel`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `media: view` to read and `media: operate` to retry or cancel.

**Good to know:** long operations return a job id instead of blocking. Poll the job rather than repeating the original request.

Library.description:
Serves the original bytes of an image in your account's library by its path.

**Use it to:**
- Fetch an original image with `GET /library/*`
- Use it where you need the untouched file rather than a rendered size, for example to download a master

**Credential:** none.

**Good to know:** for display, prefer signed `/img/*` URLs, which are resized and cached at the edge.

Live.description:
Live playback is the public address viewers' players use to watch a live channel or listen to a station.

**Use it to:**
- Play a channel's HLS or DASH output from `GET /live/{id}/master.m3u8` or `GET /live/{id}/manifest.mpd`
- Play a radio station's audio from `GET /live/{id}/stream.mp3`

**Credential:** none, or a share or playback token where the content requires one.

**Good to know:** the address only serves when the channel is on air and producing valid output. Expect 404 when off air and 503 when there is no valid content.

Me.description:
Me lets a signed-in viewer manage their own account in your app: profile, sign-in security, purchases and devices.

**Use it to:**
- Read and update the profile with `GET /api/public/me` and `PATCH /api/public/me`
- Change email, password or mobile number, and turn on two-step sign-in with the `me/email`, `me/password`, `me/phone` and `me/mfa` requests
- Show entitlements and purchases with `GET /api/public/me/entitlements` and `GET /api/public/me/purchases`
- List devices and sign out everywhere with `GET /api/public/me/sessions` and `POST /api/public/me/sign-out-everywhere`

**Credential:** viewer session (Bearer).

**Good to know:** groups and entitlements cannot be changed here. `DELETE /api/public/me` deletes the viewer's account.

Metadata Schemas.description:
Metadata schemas are named, typed sets of custom fields that you assign to VOD assets, channels and events.

**Use it to:**
- Create and edit schemas with `POST /api/metadata-schemas` and `PATCH /api/metadata-schemas/{id}`
- Use field types string, text, number, boolean, date, enum, url and tags
- See the merged fields of a schema that extends another with `GET /api/metadata-schemas/{id}/effective-fields`
- Review changes with `GET /api/metadata-schemas/{id}/history`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key. Any signed-in admin user can read, `settings: manage` is needed to change.

**Good to know:** values are validated against the assigned schema when you save a record.

Monitoring.description:
Monitoring gives one view of everything running in your account and a ranked list of what needs attention.

**Use it to:**
- See every running channel, station and event with its health with `GET /api/monitoring/live`
- Get the ranked list of problems (health, failed jobs, QC, stale publications, capacity) with `GET /api/monitoring/overview`
- Read the recent activity feed with `GET /api/monitoring/feed`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `monitoring: view`.

**Good to know:** each view is one request for the whole account, so poll these instead of fetching each channel.

Notification Templates.description:
Notification templates are reusable message layouts for the notifications Volt sends to your team.

**Use it to:**
- List templates with `GET /api/notification-templates`
- Create, edit and delete templates with `POST /api/notification-templates`, `PATCH /api/notification-templates/{id}` and `DELETE /api/notification-templates/{id}`
- Use a template when sending through the Notifications service

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `settings: view` to read and `settings: manage` to change.

**Good to know:** deleting a template does not change notifications already sent with it.

Notifications.description:
Notifications send messages to your team by email, in-app inbox or push, and keep a record of each delivery.

**Use it to:**
- Send a notification, optionally from a template, with `POST /api/notifications`, and review sends with `GET /api/notifications`
- Retry failed deliveries with `POST /api/notifications/deliveries/{id}/retry`
- Register push devices (iOS, Android, web) with `POST /api/notifications/devices`
- Read and clear the in-app inbox with `GET /api/notifications/inbox` and `POST /api/notifications/inbox/read-all`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key. Any signed-in admin user can read, the operator tier or above is needed to send or change.

**Good to know:** use `POST /api/notifications/test` to check a channel before relying on it.

Output Profiles.description:
Output profiles define how a live stream is delivered: rendition ladder, HLS and/or DASH packaging, transcode or package-only workflow, DVR window and retention.

**Use it to:**
- List profiles with `GET /api/output-profiles`
- Create a profile with `POST /api/output-profiles`
- Delete a profile with `DELETE /api/output-profiles/{id}`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key. Any signed-in admin user can read, `settings: manage` is needed to change.

**Good to know:** a channel group uses one output profile, so its channels share these settings.

Payments.description:
Payments connects your payment providers to Volt so that verified purchases grant viewers access to premium content.

**Use it to:**
- Verify an app store receipt or provider token from your app with `POST /api/public/payments/verify`
- Connect providers and map products with `PUT /api/payments/providers/{provider}` and `PATCH /api/payments/products/{id}`
- Look up a viewer's purchases with `GET /api/payments/viewers/{externalId}`
- Grant access by hand or record an outside payment with `POST /api/payments/grants` and `POST /api/payments/manual`

**Credential:** publishable key plus viewer session for verify. Management uses an admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `payments: view` to read and `payments: manage` to change.

**Good to know:** nothing is granted on an unverified event. `/api/payments/verify` is an older alias.

Plan.description:
The plan sets how many channels and stations your account may have and how many may run at once.

**Use it to:**
- Read the plan, current use and how it is shared between groups with `GET /api/plan`
- Change limits, where permitted, with `PATCH /api/plan`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key. Any signed-in admin user can read. Changes are limited to the people the response says may make them.

**Good to know:** the plan cannot go below what is in use or what groups have been given, so lower a group's allocation first.

Player.description:
The player API is what the embeddable Volt player (or your own) calls from your website or app to start playback and show what is on.

**Use it to:**
- Start playback in one request with `POST /api/public/player/session`
- Show the current track or programme with `POST /api/public/player/now-playing` and the guide with `GET /api/public/player/epg`
- Get an event's phase (pre, live, ended, replay, cancelled) with `GET /api/public/player/event`
- Send batched player telemetry with `POST /api/public/player/events`

**Credential:** publishable key or player token. Calls are also checked against the app's allowed origins.

**Good to know:** telemetry is capped at 50 events per call. The `/api/player/*` paths are older aliases.

Player Config.description:
Player configuration controls how the embeddable Volt player looks and behaves for each channel.

**Use it to:**
- Read a channel's player settings with `GET /api/player-config/{channelId}`
- Save new settings with `PUT /api/player-config/{channelId}`
- Check what the embedded player is reporting with `GET /api/player-config/{channelId}/report`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `apps: view` to read and `apps: manage` to change.

**Good to know:** players pick up these settings through `POST /api/public/player/session`, so there is nothing to change in the embed code.

Publications.description:
Publications record where each VOD asset has been published and the view counts reported back.

**Use it to:**
- List publications and their view counts with `GET /api/publications`
- Publish an asset to your portal with `POST /api/publications/vod/{id}/publish`
- Refresh view counts from the platforms with `POST /api/publications/sync-views`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `vod: view` to read, `vod: operate` to publish and `vod: manage` to sync.

**Good to know:** for social platforms, use the Social service to publish.

Publish Targets.description:
Publish targets are the destinations your VOD assets can be sent to, such as linked YouTube, Facebook, X, TikTok or Dailymotion accounts and your portal.

**Use it to:**
- List configured targets with `GET /api/publish-targets`
- Add a target with `POST /api/publish-targets`
- Rename, change or remove a target with `PATCH /api/publish-targets/{id}` and `DELETE /api/publish-targets/{id}`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `settings: view` to read and `settings: manage` to change.

**Good to know:** to link a social account through the platform's own sign-in, use `POST /api/social/connect/{platform}`.

Publishing Rules.description:
Publishing rules set what an asset gets by default (where it is published and on what terms), from account level down to content type or owner.

**Use it to:**
- List every rule with `GET /api/publishing-rules` and your publishing points with `GET /api/publishing-rules/points`
- Create or replace the rule for one level with `PUT /api/publishing-rules/{scopeKind}/{scopeId}`
- See what an asset would get, and from which rule, with `GET /api/publishing-rules/resolve`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `settings: view` to read and `settings: manage` to change.

**Good to know:** the account rule always exists and cannot be deleted. More specific rules override it.

Radio.description:
Radio covers audio-only stations: their pipeline, on-air state, levels, now-playing metadata and timed content log.

**Use it to:**
- List stations and open one with `GET /api/radio` and `GET /api/radio/{id}`
- Start, stop and put a station on air with `POST /api/radio/{id}/start`, `.../stop` and `.../air`
- Read now playing, levels, QC and the log with `GET /api/radio/{id}/nowplaying`, `.../levels`, `.../qc` and `.../log`
- Check a source before using it with `POST /api/radio/probe`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `radio: view` to read, `radio: operate` to start, stop or air and `radio: manage` to change.

**Good to know:** stations are channels too, so groups, recording, EPG and access rules apply to them unchanged.

Recordings.description:
Recordings are the raw captures of your live output: one per event run, and one per calendar day for each continuous channel.

**Use it to:**
- List and open recordings with `GET /api/recordings` and `GET /api/recordings/{id}`
- Publish a whole recording as VOD with `POST /api/recordings/{id}/publish`, or clip a time range with `POST /api/recordings/{id}/clip`
- Download an MP4 with `GET /api/recordings/{id}/download`
- Read the timeline, waveform, transcript and programmes with `GET /api/recordings/{id}/timeline` and related requests

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `recordings: view` to read, `recordings: operate` to publish and `recordings: manage` to compose clips.

**Good to know:** clips and downloads answer 409 `no_media`, with the gaps, when nothing was recorded in the range. Downloads answer 202 while exporting.

Reports.description:
Operating reports say, for each channel, station and event, every time it ran, how long for, how long it was on air, why each run ended, and what the audience did. Built for SLA reviews and monthly client reporting.

**Use it to:**
- Read one stream's report with `GET /api/reports/stream/{id}?from=&to=`
- Download it as a spreadsheet with `GET /api/reports/stream/{id}.csv`, one row per run plus a TOTAL row
- Summarise every stream for a period with `GET /api/reports/streams`, filtered by `kind` and `q` and sorted with `sort=-hours_run`
- Download the period summary with `GET /api/reports/streams.csv`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `analytics: view`.

**Good to know:** a null figure means "not known", never zero. An exact per-run peak exists only while raw viewing sessions are retained; older runs report `peak_basis: not_retained` with the day's peak beside it. Reports survive deleting the stream, and historical rows keep the name the stream ran under.

Scheduled Clips.description:
Scheduled clips are clipping windows set on a live timeline. When the window ends, Volt cuts it into a VOD asset.

**Use it to:**
- List clipping windows with `GET /api/scheduled-clips`
- Schedule a clip, choosing a manifest, progressive or both, with `POST /api/scheduled-clips`
- Cancel a clip that has not been cut yet with `DELETE /api/scheduled-clips/{id}`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `recordings: view` to read and `recordings: manage` to change.

**Good to know:** a clip can only be cancelled while it is still scheduled.

Search.description:
Search finds channels, radio stations, events and recordings in your account by name or title.

**Use it to:**
- Run one search across your account with `GET /api/search`
- Back a site-wide search box in your own admin tools
- Use each result's kind to link to the right record

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, any signed-in admin user.

Share.description:
The share page is what a share link's recipient opens: a standalone page that plays the shared asset and offers permitted downloads.

**Use it to:**
- Open the recipient page with `GET /share/{token}`
- Get the page's data and a playback token with `POST /api/share/{token}/resolve`
- Send an access code by email with `POST /api/share/{token}/request-code`
- Download a permitted element with `GET /api/share/{token}/download/{element}`

**Credential:** the share link token, plus a PIN or emailed code when the link has one.

**Good to know:** these requests never accept an admin credential and never reach any other asset.

Share Links.description:
Share links give someone outside your account a private link to one asset, optionally protected by a PIN or emailed code.

**Use it to:**
- Create a link with `POST /api/share-links`
- List links and see their views with `GET /api/share-links` and `GET /api/share-links/{id}`
- End a link at once with `POST /api/share-links/{id}/revoke`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `sharing: view` to read and `sharing: manage` to change.

**Good to know:** the link URL is returned once, at creation. Each link reaches exactly one asset.

Social.description:
Social publishing sends your VOD assets to linked social accounts and tracks each post.

**Use it to:**
- See which platforms are available with `GET /api/social/platforms` and link an account with `POST /api/social/connect/{platform}`
- Publish an asset to one or more accounts with `POST /api/social/publish/{assetId}` (prefill from `GET /api/social/publish/{assetId}/defaults`)
- Follow, retry or take down posts with `GET /api/social/publications` and the `retry` and `remove` requests
- Refresh view counts with `POST /api/social/sync-views`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `vod: view` to read, `vod: operate` to publish or retry and `vod: manage` to link, remove or sync.

**Good to know:** a sandbox account (`POST /api/social/sandbox/{platform}`) behaves like a platform without posting, for testing.

Social Sandbox.description:
Shows what a post to a sandbox social account would look like, without anything being posted to a real platform.

**Use it to:**
- Open the preview of a sandbox post with `GET /social-sandbox/{id}`
- Check titles, descriptions and media before publishing for real
- Create the sandbox account first with `POST /api/social/sandbox/{platform}`, then publish to it as usual

**Credential:** admin session.

**Good to know:** sandbox posts never leave Volt, and their view counts are not real.
Social Sandbox.hiddenReason: test-only preview of sandbox social posts

Source Preview.description:
Source preview relays a channel's HLS input so the console can play it even when the source does not allow cross-site playback.

**Use it to:**
- Play the relayed input from `GET /api/source-preview/{token}/index.m3u8`
- Let the player follow the rewritten playlist and segment addresses (`.../pl` and `.../seg`)

**Credential:** the preview token in the address, issued for an input you can see.

**Good to know:** the relay only fetches addresses from that input's own playlists.
Source Preview.hiddenReason: console helper; preview tokens are issued by the Volt console

Sources.description:
Sources helps you check a contribution feed before you attach it to a channel, station or event.

**Use it to:**
- Probe a source address and protocol and see what it is sending with `POST /api/sources/probe`
- Read an HLS playlist (master variants and renditions, or a media playlist) with `POST /api/sources/hls`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `manage` on `channels`, `radio` or `events`.

**Good to know:** `POST /api/sources/hls` reads the playlist text only, so it is quick enough to call as the address is typed.

Status.description:
Status reports the latest state and event log of each live channel and event, by polling or as a live push.

**Use it to:**
- Poll the status of every stream with `GET /api/status`
- Read one stream and its event log with `GET /api/status/{kind}/{id}` and `GET /api/status/{kind}/{id}/events`
- Receive changes within about a second over server-sent events with `GET /api/status/stream`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `monitoring: view`. The live stream also accepts a `?ticket=` for EventSource.

**Good to know:** open one live stream per viewer screen, not one per channel.

Storage.description:
Storage shows what media your account holds, where it lives, whether it can be read now, and what the retention rules will do to it next.

**Use it to:**
- Check what your storage supports with `GET /api/storage/capabilities`
- List media objects with `GET /api/storage/objects`, and hold or restore one with `POST /api/storage/objects/{id}/hold` and `.../restore`
- Set retention rules with `PUT /api/storage/retention`, preview them with `POST /api/storage/retention/preview`, and see the effective result with `GET /api/storage/retention/effective`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `media: view` to read and `media: manage` to change.

**Good to know:** read capabilities first. Archive tiers and restore are only offered where storage supports them.

Thumbnails.description:
Thumbnails provides stills and sprite sheets of your channels and events for hover previews, scrubbing and clip thumbnails.

**Use it to:**
- Get sprite sheets for a time span with `GET /api/thumbnails/storyboard`
- Get WebVTT thumbnail tracks with `GET /api/thumbnails/vtt`, `GET /api/thumbnails/recordings/{id}.vtt` and `GET /api/thumbnails/vod/{id}.vtt`
- Check which hours are built with `GET /api/thumbnails/status`, and build older hours with `POST /api/thumbnails/build`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key. Any signed-in admin user can read, the operator tier or above is needed to build.

**Good to know:** a storyboard request covers at most 48 hours and defaults to the last hour.

Tickets.description:
Tickets let your team raise support requests with the Volt team and follow their progress.

**Use it to:**
- List your account's tickets with `GET /api/tickets`
- Raise a ticket, with a priority, with `POST /api/tickets`
- Follow one ticket with `GET /api/tickets/{id}`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key. Any signed-in admin user can read, the operator tier or above is needed to raise one.

Uploads.description:
Uploads move media files into Volt in chunks, so large files can resume after an interruption.

**Use it to:**
- Open an upload session with `POST /api/uploads`, and list or abandon sessions with `GET /api/uploads` and `DELETE /api/uploads/{id}`
- Send each chunk with `PUT /api/uploads/{id}/chunks/{index}`
- Check progress with `GET /api/uploads/{id}/state`, then complete with `POST /api/uploads/{id}/finish`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key to open and list, with `media: view` to read and `media: manage` to change. Chunks and finish use the upload session token returned when the session opens.

**Good to know:** send chunk bodies as raw bytes, not JSON. The session token only works for its own upload.

Uploads (tus).description:
A resumable upload endpoint that follows the open tus protocol, for clients that already speak tus.

**Use it to:**
- Create an upload with `POST /api/tus`, passing the file name, type and optional metadata in `Upload-Metadata`
- Send bytes with `PATCH /api/tus/{id}` and check the offset with `HEAD /api/tus/{id}`
- Abandon an upload with `DELETE /api/tus/{id}`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key on every request, with `media: manage`.

**Good to know:** a tus upload is an ordinary upload session, so it follows your ingest rules like any other.

User Groups.description:
The original address for access roles. It manages the same named sets of feature access levels as the Access roles service.

**Use it to:**
- List roles and member counts with `GET /api/user-groups`
- Create, edit, copy or delete roles with `POST /api/user-groups`, `PATCH /api/user-groups/{id}` and `POST /api/user-groups/{id}/copy`
- Read the feature list with `GET /api/user-groups/catalogue`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `access: view` (or `users: view`) to read and `access: manage` to change.

**Good to know:** prefer `/api/access-roles` for new integrations. Both addresses act on the same roles.

Users.description:
Users are your own staff who sign in to Volt, with their roles, status and two-step sign-in.

**Use it to:**
- List and open users with `GET /api/users` and `GET /api/users/{id}`
- Add, change or remove users with `POST /api/users`, `PATCH /api/users/{id}` and `DELETE /api/users/{id}`
- Reset a locked-out user's two-step sign-in with `POST /api/users/{id}/mfa/reset`
- Require two-step sign-in for everyone with `PUT /api/users/security-policy`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `users: view` to read and `users: manage` to change. The security policy also needs the admin tier.

**Good to know:** you cannot change yourself, someone above your tier, or someone whose access you do not fully hold.

VOD.description:
VOD assets are your on-demand videos, from recordings, clips or uploads, with their metadata, review state and availability.

**Use it to:**
- List and open assets with `GET /api/vod` and `GET /api/vod/{id}`, and edit metadata with `PUT /api/vod/{id}`
- Review, QC and trim with `POST /api/vod/{id}/review`, `POST /api/vod/{id}/qc` and `PATCH /api/vod/{id}/trim`
- Publish or withdraw with `POST /api/vod/{id}/publish` and `POST /api/vod/{id}/withdraw`, and set availability with `PATCH /api/vod/{id}/availability`
- Get schema.org JSON-LD for SEO with `GET /api/vod/{id}/schema.org`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `vod: view` to read, `vod: operate` to publish or withdraw and `vod: manage` to change.

**Good to know:** metadata is validated against the asset's assigned schema.

Viewers.description:
Viewers are the public users of your apps, as your team sees them for support and access management.

**Use it to:**
- Find viewers with `GET /api/viewers` and open one, with entitlements and sessions, with `GET /api/viewers/{id}`
- Change a viewer's groups or status with `PATCH /api/viewers/{id}`
- Sign a viewer out everywhere or reset their two-step sign-in with `POST /api/viewers/{id}/sign-out` and `.../mfa/reset`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `viewers: view` to read, `viewers: operate` to sign out and `viewers: manage` to change.

**Good to know:** to grant paid access, use `POST /api/payments/grants`.

Watchfolders.description:
Watchfolders pick up files dropped into a folder and ingest them by your ordered rules, with a review queue for refused files.

**Use it to:**
- Create and edit folders with `POST /api/watchfolders` and `PATCH /api/watchfolders/{id}`
- Add and order rules with `POST /api/watchfolders/{id}/rules` and `PATCH /api/watchfolders/{id}/rules/{ruleId}`
- Test a file name without moving anything with `POST /api/watchfolders/{id}/dry-run`, or scan now with `POST /api/watchfolders/{id}/scan`
- Reprocess or remove refused files with `GET /api/watchfolders/{id}/items` and `.../resolve`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `media: view` to read, `media: operate` to dry-run and `media: manage` to change.

**Good to know:** use the dry run before changing rules on a busy folder.

Workflows.description:
Workflows show how work moves through Volt and which add-ons run at each stage, with a record of every run.

**Use it to:**
- See the stages, hooks and attached add-ons with `GET /api/workflows/map`
- List and open runs with `GET /api/workflows/runs` and `GET /api/workflows/runs/{id}`
- Run an add-on by hand, cancel or retry with `POST /api/workflows/runs` and the `cancel` and `retry` requests
- Trace what happened to one item with `GET /api/workflows/trace`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `settings: view` to read and `settings: operate` to run, cancel or retry.

**Good to know:** a retry creates a new run with the same add-on, subject and options.

XMLTV.description:
XMLTV partner feeds publish your programme guide at a private URL for PVRs, IPTV middleware and guide aggregators to poll.

**Use it to:**
- Give a partner a feed URL of the form `GET /xmltv/{token}.xml` (or `.xml.gz`)
- Create, rescope, rotate or revoke feeds with `POST /api/epg/xmltv/feeds` and related requests

**Credential:** the feed token in the URL, no headers needed.

**Good to know:** rotate a feed's token if its URL leaks. The old URL stops working.

Timeline.description:
Timeline gives the Live Streams page's Past, Now, Next view: every stream on one clock, in one request.

**Use it to:**
- Draw what aired, what is on now and what is next across all your streams with `GET /api/timeline/grid`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `monitoring: view`, and `view` on channels, radio or events for those rows.

**Good to know:** the window is capped at 48 hours and rows page at 50. For one stream in detail use `GET /api/channels/:id/timeline` and `/coverage`.

Fast.description:
FAST channels play a scheduled lineup of your media as a continuous linear channel, with ad breaks decided by your ad servers.

**Use it to:**
- Create and list FAST channels with `POST /api/fast/channels` and `GET /api/fast/channels`
- Build, preview and activate a lineup with `POST /api/fast/channels/:id/lineups`, `POST /api/fast/lineups/:lid/preview` and `POST /api/fast/lineups/:lid/activate`
- Prepare a channel and put it on air with `POST /api/fast/channels/:id/prepare` and `POST /api/fast/channels/:id/on-air`
- Connect VAST ad servers with `POST /api/fast/ad-servers`, check one with `POST /api/fast/ad-servers/:sid/test`, and set a channel's ad mode with `PUT /api/fast/channels/:id/ads`
- Read how breaks were filled with `GET /api/fast/channels/:id/ad-report`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key. Reading needs any signed-in admin user, changes need operator tier or above.

**Good to know:** ad decisions are fetched ahead of each break, never while a player is loading the manifest.

Graphics.description:
Graphics manages HTML overlay templates (scorebugs, lower thirds, sponsor bugs, tickers) and runs them live on your channels and events.

**Use it to:**
- Import, edit and publish templates with `POST /api/graphics/templates/import`, `PUT /api/graphics/templates/:id/draft` and `POST /api/graphics/templates/:id/draft/publish`
- Connect the data that fills them with `POST /api/graphics/sources` and push values with `POST /api/graphics/sources/:id/push`
- Group templates into setups and assign them to streams with `POST /api/graphics/setups` and `POST /api/graphics/assignments`
- Take graphics on and off air with `POST /api/graphics/assignments/:id/air`, or run an event's rundown with `POST /api/graphics/rundowns/:eventId/take`
- See what is live and what changed with `GET /api/graphics/live` and `GET /api/graphics/log`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `graphics: view` to read, `graphics: operate` to run graphics live and `graphics: manage` to change templates and setups.

**Good to know:** a published template version never changes. Edit the draft and publish again to make a new version.

Live Streams.description:
Live streams gives one view of any live channel, radio station or event, whatever kind it is.

**Use it to:**
- Read a stream as one record, with its production and distribution settings, with `GET /api/live-streams/:kind/:id`
- Publish it as schema.org JSON-LD (a VideoObject from a BroadcastEvent) for search engines and partners with `GET /api/live-streams/:kind/:id/schema.org`
- Read what a source provider sends for it with `GET /api/live-streams/:kind/:id/provider`
- List the stream presets (live channel, live event, FAST channel, premiere, loop) with `GET /api/live-streams/presets`

**Credential:** admin session (Bearer) or account secret key, with `monitoring: view`.

**Good to know:** `:kind` is `channel`, `radio` or `event`. The preset is worked out from the stream's settings and is not stored.

Gfx.description:
Graphics delivery serves the files of a published graphics template version to the player and overlay that show it.

**Use it to:**
- Load a template version's files with `GET /gfx/:versionId/*`

**Credential:** none, share token or playback token. These are public delivery files.

**Good to know:** files are served sandboxed and can only connect to the template's own package. Versions never change, so they cache well.

GET /api/vod.description: The account's on-demand library: recordings published as VOD, clips, uploads and watch-folder files. Search titles and file names with `q`, filter on any field below (for example `review_state=in_review` or `published=true`), and sort with `sort=-created_at`.

GET /api/recordings.description: Raw captures of live output, newest first. `q` searches titles and source names, then the programme on air and the transcript. Filter by `channel_id`, `kind`, `status` or time (`start_epoch_ms[gte]=...`).

GET /api/jobs.description: Background work (encodes, imports, conversions) with its state. Typical: `state=failed,cancelled&created_at[gte]=2026-10-17` to find what went wrong today.

GET /api/timeline/grid.summary: Get the timeline grid (Past, Now, Next)
GET /api/timeline/grid.description:
Every stream the caller can see as one row on a shared clock, for the Live Streams Timeline view: programmes (as-run times preferred over scheduled), the media actually recorded with its gaps (past part of the window only, measured from disk), clip ticks, and the same five-gate status the Live board shows. One call for the whole grid instead of one per stream.

`from` and `to` are ISO 8601 (epoch ms also accepted); the window is capped at 48 hours and a wider one is a 400. `kinds` narrows to `channel,radio,event,loop` (rows of a kind your role cannot view are absent, not empty). Rows page at 50 with the list standard's cursor: follow `next` in the body or the `Link: rel="next"` header.
